name: crodh mara

attributes.attribute: kept by fairies in the ocean deeps
came ashore to mate with mortal cows
often red, sometimes gray or dun

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Highlanders of Scotland called this mythological animal crodh mara. They believed hornless supernatural cattle belonged to the fairies and dwelt in the ocean deeps. The cattle could leave the sea and pair with ordinary cows. The pairing bettered the herds of the land. The cattle usually carried a red coat, a color shared by many fairy beasts. Sometimes they appeared gray or dun in color.

okr.objective: crodh mara are fairy cattle of the Scottish ocean deeps.
key_results: Highlanders of Scotland believed fairies kept these hornless cattle at sea.
The cattle came ashore to mate with mortal cows and bettered earthly herds.
They were often red and sometimes seen as gray or dun.
